name: Safety Core Control Contract
preconditions: The caller has authority to submit the bounded request but does not gain execution authority from submission.
Inputs use supported version 0.2.0 and contain no raw secret or credential payload.
Filesystem operations identify an explicit source or destination root.
The configured policy and any supplied evidence pass structural validation.
obligations: Safety Core validates all mandatory fields before any filesystem side effect.
Safety Core computes risk deterministically and fails closed on missing or contradictory evidence.
Safety Core never executes the governed business action.
Safety Core records minimized decision evidence when an audit ledger is configured.
Reopening an existing audit ledger for append requires an independently retained expected record count and head hash.
The caller treats review as non-executable and remains accountable for authorization and execution.
Backup and recovery reject traversal, symlinks, unsafe members, and overwrite.
postconditions: A decision contains request identity, policy version, risk evidence, status, and ordered reasons.
An allow result means only that declared Safety gates passed at evaluation time.
A recovery result identifies only newly created, hash-verified files.
Incident transitions retain prior history and revision.
failure_semantics: Malformed or unsupported input is rejected explicitly.
Missing mandatory evidence yields deny or review, never allow.
Ledger corruption or append failure prevents a recorded allow result.
Unsafe archive or path input stops before destination writes.
An invalid incident transition leaves the prior incident unchanged.
